attributes.measurements: Both landed fixes were found by reading fnasm --diff windows directly (not guessing from --ops line numbers alone) and mapping target's ACTUAL branch topology back to source: in both cases target's disassembly shows the LARGER of two sibling if/else bodies placed as the unconditional fallthrough (no branch needed to reach it) with the smaller body relocated to a far target reached only by a taken conditional branch, while our then-current source (which wrote the smaller body as the textual 'if' arm) compiled with the natural default layout (if-true falls through inline, else is the jump-away target) -- i.e. our SMALL body was inline and BIG body was jump-away, the mirror image of target. Swapping which condition is tested (De Morgan negation, zero semantic change, verified by re-deriving the negated condition algebraically and confirming no other reference to the original condition polarity existed in either arm) reliably flips MWCC's fallthrough choice to match. A third, smaller-scope test of the SAME hypothesis on a plain (non-nested) ternary `hit = damage == 0 ? 2 : 3` (T[960:961]@f00-f04, target beq-to-far / ours bne-to-far) was tried (`damage != 0 ? 3 : 2`) and made ZERO byte difference -- confirming the arm-swap lever only fires on genuine if/else STATEMENT bodies (which the compiler must lay out as separate basic blocks), not on a simple ternary EXPRESSION (which MWCC evidently canonicalizes to one fixed branch polarity regardless of source spelling); reverted to the more natural `== 0 ? 2 : 3` phrasing since neutral. A companion residual noted in both landed clusters and in the still-open CritterDamage `hit<0/==0/else` 3-way chain (T[1580:1602]@ pre-fix, now branch-aligned but retaining one extra target-only 'mr r29,r0' merge instruction ours lacks) was independently probed with the SAME hit-chain rewritten as both an explicit ternary and a nested if/else -- both produced byte-IDENTICAL output to each other, confirming ternary-vs-if/else spelling is compiler-normalized for a simple 2-way scalar assignment merge (the remaining 'mr' is a register-allocation artifact, not a source-shape lever, and was left as an accepted single-instruction residual after the outer if/else polarity fix landed cleanly).
